subject: Governing law / temporary injunctive relief — PioneerHealth MSA redlines
body:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@pioneerhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: megan.li@pioneerhealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PioneerHealth - MSA redlines (governing law / injunctions)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've shared the internal redlines with our legal team and attached them here (Pioneer_MSA_redlines_AlexTorres.pdf). High level asks from Pioneer:

- Governing law: they want California law retained.
- Venue for disputes: they prefer courts in San Mateo County (local state court) — their outside counsel is asking for local-court access.
- Emergency injunctive relief: they want an explicit carveout that allows Pioneer to seek temporary injunctions in local courts without waiting for arbitration. They also want a short notice / meet-and-confer before filing where feasible.
- Arbitration: they accept arbitration for final remedy but want the pre-arbitration step clarified so it doesn't block urgent court relief.

We're trying to move quickly — can you flag any must-have objections from your side? If you can propose specific compromise language for the injunction carveout, that will help speed procurement.

Attachments: Pioneer_MSA_redlines_AlexTorres.pdf (redline PDF)

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Head of Tech Contracts
PioneerHealth

Subject: RE: PioneerHealth - MSA redlines (governing law / injunctions)

Team — looping you in for legal sync. Alex attached Pioneer’s redlines (see PDF). Key asks summarized above. My take:

- Governing law in CA is OK for us (no strong pushback).
- Venue: we should avoid a strict county-specific venue; instead, accept courts in California with a default for federal district or state courts sitting in Santa Clara / San Mateo counties if feasible. County specificity creates ops risk for enforcement.
- Emergency injunctive relief: we should accept a narrow carveout that permits either party to seek injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction (to preserve urgent customer protections), but limit forum-selection to "courts located in California" to avoid overseas filing. Also add a clause requiring a 48-hour notice/meet-and-confer except where not practicable.
- Arbitration: recommend arbitration for all non-emergency disputes with AAA (or JAMS) in San Francisco, CA.

I've attached our internal quick playbook on injunctive carveouts (Injunction_playbook_v1.docx) — see section 2 for suggested language.

Can Legal propose a short clause we can offer back to Pioneer? Also confirm whether finance wants any escrow or security language flagged.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
(kimberly_park@redwood.ai)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.torres@pioneerhealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: PioneerHealth - MSA redlines (governing law / injunctions)

Kim / Laura — quick legal viewpoint and proposed compromise clause below.

Summary: Redwood is willing to accept California governing law and an emergency-relief carveout so long as the carveout is limited and does not create an open door to forum-shopping. We should:

1) Agree governing law = California.
2) For ordinary remedies, require arbitration in San Francisco (AAA) as Kimberly suggested.
3) For emergency injunctive relief, allow either party to seek interim equitable relief in a court of competent jurisdiction, but:
   - Limit venue to "courts located in the State of California" (so not any county worldwide).
   - Add a mandatory, but short, meet-and-confer period (48 hours) unless urgent relief is required (e.g., immediate risk to safety or data exfiltration).
   - Require Redwood to provide a covenant in the clause that it will use injunction rights only to preserve the status quo and not for ordinary contract remedies.

Proposed draft clause (short form):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may seek temporary injunctive or other equitable relief in the state or federal courts located in the State of California to preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect Confidential Information. Except in circumstances where immediate relief is necessary to prevent imminent harm, the party seeking such relief shall provide the other party with at least 48 hours' prior written notice and a reasonable opportunity to meet and confer. The parties agree that non-emergency disputes shall be resolved by binding arbitration in San Francisco, California under the rules of the American Arbitration Association."

We should avoid specifying a single county; "courts located in the State of California" gives them the local access they want while keeping flexibility for Redwood enforcement.

I will prepare a tracked-redline to the PDF and upload the clause. If this approach is acceptable to Sales, we can send the clause as Redwood’s counter-proposal and ask them to confirm.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

---
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@pioneerhealth.com>, Megan Li <megan.li@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: PioneerHealth - MSA redlines (governing law / injunctions)

Alex / Megan — appreciate the quick turnaround. Thanks for sharing Pioneer’s redlines.

We want to move this forward and propose the following compromise to balance Pioneer’s need for local court access and Redwood’s enforcement/operational needs:

1) Governing law: California (agreed).
2) Arbitration: binding arbitration for all non-emergency disputes, administered by AAA in San Francisco, California.
3) Emergency injunctive relief carveout: either party may seek temporary injunctive or other equitable relief in state or federal courts located in the State of California to preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect Confidential Information. Except where immediate relief is necessary, the party seeking such relief will provide at least 48 hours' prior written notice and a reasonable opportunity to meet-and-confer.

This keeps their ability to get quick court relief but limits forum-shopping and creates a short pre-filing notice we ask them to honor. Please let us know whether Pioneer can accept the text above. If yes, we’ll produce a tracked-redline and send a DocuSign packet for signatures.

Attachments (for reference): Pioneer_MSA_redlines_AlexTorres.pdf (we received), Injunction_playbook_v1.docx (internal).

Next steps:
- If you accept the language, confirm by EOD Wednesday and we’ll prepare the redline for signature.
- If Pioneer needs county-level specificity, flag why it’s critical so we can escalate to Execs for approval.

Best,
Kimberly Park
